cards.front: What is the primary goal of physical education?
cards.back: To develop physical fitness, motor skills, and promote healthy lifestyles

cards.front: What are the five components of physical fitness?
cards.back: Cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, and body composition

cards.front: What is cardiovascular endurance?
cards.back: The ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen to working muscles during sustained activity

cards.front: What is muscular strength?
cards.back: The maximum amount of force a muscle can produce in a single effort

cards.front: What is muscular endurance?
cards.back: The ability of muscles to perform repeated contractions over time

cards.front: What is flexibility?
cards.back: The range of motion around a joint

cards.front: What is body composition?
cards.back: The ratio of fat mass to lean mass in the body

cards.front: What is the FITT principle?
cards.back: Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type - the four elements of exercise prescription

cards.front: What is the recommended frequency for cardiovascular exercise?
cards.back: 3-5 times per week for optimal health benefits

cards.front: What is the recommended duration for cardiovascular exercise?
cards.back: 20-60 minutes per session for health benefits

cards.front: What is the target heart rate zone?
cards.back: 60-80% of maximum heart rate for cardiovascular fitness

cards.front: How do you calculate maximum heart rate?
cards.back: 220 minus your age in years

cards.front: What is the difference between aerobic and anaerobic exercise?
cards.back: Aerobic uses oxygen for energy (endurance), while anaerobic doesn't use oxygen (short bursts)

cards.front: What is the importance of warming up before exercise?
cards.back: To prepare the body for activity, increase blood flow, and reduce injury risk

cards.front: What is the importance of cooling down after exercise?
cards.back: To gradually return the body to rest, prevent blood pooling, and reduce muscle soreness

cards.front: What is the importance of stretching?
cards.back: To improve flexibility, reduce muscle tension, and prevent injury

cards.front: What is the difference between static and dynamic stretching?
cards.back: Static stretching holds positions, while dynamic stretching involves movement

cards.front: What is the importance of hydration during exercise?
cards.back: To maintain performance, prevent dehydration, and regulate body temperature

cards.front: What is the importance of proper nutrition for physical activity?
cards.back: To provide energy, support recovery, and maintain health

cards.front: What is the importance of rest and recovery?
cards.back: To allow the body to repair, adapt, and prevent overtraining

cards.front: What is the importance of proper form in exercise?
cards.back: To maximize effectiveness, prevent injury, and ensure safety

cards.front: What is the importance of progression in exercise?
cards.back: To gradually increase intensity and challenge the body for continued improvement

cards.front: What is the importance of variety in exercise?

cards.back: To achieve and maintain fitness goals and health benefits
